disclaimer: This directory was compiled with AI (Claude) assistance from publicly available sources. It is incomplete: it covers 132 of roughly 198 ABA-accredited US law schools, and the gap is systematic — the original pass worked alphabetically by state and stopped after New York, so later states are underrepresented. Two things to read carefully before drawing conclusions from a tier chip. First, a 'none' or 'standalone' tier means the parent university runs no research-computing resource; it does not mean no compute, because NSF ACCESS allocates national supercomputing time to any researcher at a US academic institution in any field at no cost. Second, a high tier does not guarantee law-school access: some centers list the schools they serve, and Law is not always among them. Rows whose notes begin 'Re-verified', 'RECLASSIFIED', 'CORRECTED', 'UPDATED' or 'ADDED' have been through the deep pass.
